title: VisionWebDev: A Hierarchical Benchmark for Visual Website Development with Agent Verification
claim: A benchmark spans hierarchical task levels, an agent that produces outputs, and a workflow-based verification that scores them.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, big arrows between stages, stacked levels in first panel
description: Three rounded panels run left to right, joined by large blue arrows. The left blue panel, 'Hierarchical Task Formulation', stacks three boxes bottom-to-top with upward arrows: Level 1 static webpage (multi-device prototypes to responsive HTML/CSS), Level 2 interactive frontend (linked pages and inter-page logic to interactive output), and Level 3 full-stack website (requirements, DB and assets to a full-stack system). The middle green panel, 'Coding Agent', shows a robot with code bubbles, an image and a video icon, labelled 'Coding Agent + Multimodal Resources'. A down arrow leads to a generated website shown as devices and a database. The right panel, 'Workflow-based Agent Verification', shows a graph of test workflows with functional nodes (orange circles F1–F6) and visual nodes (blue squares V1–V2). Below it a GUI agent verifier and a VLM judge produce a functional score and a visual score.
caption: Overview of \benchname{}, a hierarchical benchmark for visual website development. Tasks span three levels—static webpages, interactive frontends, and full-stack websites—requiring agents to integrate visual prototypes with textual specifications. Evaluation is performed via a workflow-based agent verification paradigm, measuring functional correctness and visual fidelity.
abstract: Recent advances in large language models have improved the capabilities of coding agents, yet systematic evaluation of complex, end-to-end website development remains limited. To address this gap, we introduce Vision2Web, a hierarchical benchmark for visual website development, spanning from static UI-to-code generation, interactive multi-page frontend reproduction, to long-horizon full-stack website development. The benchmark is constructed from real-world websites and comprises a total of 193 tasks across 16 categories, with 918 prototype images and 1,255 test cases. To support flexible, thorough and reliable evaluation, we propose workflow-based agent verification paradigm based on two complementary components: a GUI agent verifier and a VLM-based judge. We evaluate multiple visual language models instantiated under different coding-agent frameworks, revealing substantial performance gaps at all task levels, with state-of-the-art models still struggling on full-stack development.
